neighbours.label: a capitalised word inside a multi-word name at a slot that is normally lower case: a capitalised species epithet ('Theobroma Cacao', 'Rhinella Rostrata') or 'The' after 'of' ('Maid of The Mist'); quiet on the standard lower-case form
fire: The coffee shrub, Coffea Arabica, is native to the highlands of Ethiopia.
The grey wolf (Canis Lupus) once ranged over the whole continent.
They booked a table at the Rose of The Valley inn for Sunday.
The sunflower (Helianthus Annuus) follows the sun during the day.
The brown trout, Salmo Trutta, prefers cold and clear streams.
We watched the play at the Star of The Sea hall near the harbour.
The olive tree (Olea Europaea) can live for many centuries.
The red fox, Vulpes Vulpes, has adapted well to city life.
quiet: The coffee shrub, Coffea arabica, is native to the highlands of Ethiopia.
The grey wolf (Canis lupus) once ranged over the whole continent.
They booked a table at the rose of the valley inn for Sunday.
The sunflower follows the sun during the day.
The brown trout, Salmo trutta, prefers cold and clear streams.
We watched the play at the hall by the sea near the harbour.
The olive tree (Olea europaea) can live for many centuries.
The red fox has adapted well to city life.

notes: Card: 'بي' x4 (Arabic 'بن ابي' in names), ' The' x3, ' C', 'ata'. Probes: capitalised epithets 0.62-0.98, 'of The' 0.38-0.44; lower-case epithets and 'of the' 0.03-0.04. Arabic 'بن ابي' 0.51-0.80 also fires and is not in this test (Arabic has no case, so it does not fit the label as worded).
